It's very nice to have a filter that I can wash and reuse indefinitely. The filters that originally came with my Toddy system worked fine, but I used them way longer than I should have, and they were pretty haggard from multiple washes and dryings.

The holes on this filter are very, very small, so the concentrate takes a little longer to drain than with the default filters, and I had to jostle the coffee ground container a bit to get the concentrate to start draining, but once it got started it worked fine. I did move the ground container around a bit while it was brewing, so it's possible that the mixture got a little 'stirred', which can cause blockage. Whatever the reason, the longer, slightly irregular draining is not a deal-breaker. Glad to have this.
Works Great!
Fantastic.  I purchased our Toddy nearly 5 years ago, and needless to say, have gone through countless filters.  I just used this for the first time and wish I had known about this back in 2011.

It took hours to filter our cold brew coffee using this filter. We mix our cold brew in a separate jug and pour into the Toddy reservoir to filter. This way we avoid having most of the grounds in the reservoir, enabling a quicker filter time. Using the felt filter, we can get a gallon of coffee to filter within an hour. Using the stainless filter took seven hours to filter the same amount of coffee. I would not recommend this product.
The filter actually prevented the coffee from draining into the decanter.

This is a great idea in theory. I love that it's re-usable and uses stainless steel. However, it takes about 6 to 8 hours to filter it... which is just unacceptable. The holes are too small. It already takes 12 to 24 hours to brew cold brew... I don't want to wait another 6 to 8 hours to be able to drink it!

This filter definitely took a few frustrating times to get the hang of, but taking into account the laws of hydrodynamics, I realized that "burping" the correct way is a crucial step. You need to pre-fill with enough water before adding grounds so that you can remove the rubber stopper and release some of the pre-brewed water to prep/"burp" the filter in the correct direction before adding grounds. Then, after brewing, when you're ready to release the coffee, the filter has been sitting in the correct orientation and the coffee will flow freely through the filter. Not disturbing the grounds after adding them also helps, otherwise they will tend to get sucked towards the filter with the escaping coffee and block the filter holes.

I purchased the LG 5231JA2006A LT600P 5231JA2006B Comparable Refrigerator Water Filter 6 Pack from DiscountFilterStore and I am in no way happy with them and do not believe these filters are "New."
The 1st filter lasted a week before tasting bad, and now the 2nd filter started tasting rancid today, after only 2 weeks. What angers me more, is my 4 year old was drinking the water when he said it didn't taste right. So, I got up to taste it and low and behold, nasty water again.
Needless to say, they all have signs that a larger label was removed and a smaller Tier 1 label was attached. In addition to that, the fail rate of these filters are insane. My first Tier 1 filter experience was great, but to be 3 weeks into a 6 pack order and I'm down two, somethings not right, here. That's why I'm not convinced these are "New", but a poor recycle.
I wouldn't recommend spending $62 dollars on the 6 pack, or buying any multiple packs of these filters. I wish I would have bought one, so when it failed a week or two later, I'd been out a few dollars rather than $62....Naturally, my return by date has passed, too. Had this second filter gone bad 3 or 4 days ago, I could have and definitely would have returned or at least had the option to open a ticket. I won't stick any of the last four in my fridge, especially after what happened tonight with my 4 year old!!!
